candidates.summary: a directory link with a trailing slash maps to the live site even though that directory page is in the snapshot
candidates.failure_scenario: Seeds() captures the directory page at "/r/gnoland" (no trailing slash) and writes it to r/gnoland/index.html. Every gnoweb link to a directory carries the slash - components/views/directory.html:28 emits `Browse`. mapURL keys c.pages on the exact string, so canonicalURL("/r/gnoland/") misses the "/r/gnoland" key and the link falls through to c.Live: the rewritten page ships `href="https://gno.land/r/gnoland/"`. A reviewer clicking Browse in the preview of a PR-added realm leaves the preview for gno.land, where that realm does not exist. inScope:191 refuses trailing-slash URLs too, so the page is never captured under that key either, which makes urlToFile's _dir branch (crawl.go:496-498) unreachable dead code despite TestURLToFileIsSafe and TestSplitURLKeepsTrailingSlash pinning the two forms apart.
candidates.verify_by: go test -run TestReachCapturedDirectoryIsLinkedOffsite -v .  in misc/gnopreview with the artifact copied in; expect mapURL("/r/gnoland/") to resolve inside the snapshot, observe "https://gno.land/r/gnoland/"
candidates.evidence: captured directory page file: r/gnoland/index.html | mapURL("/r/gnoland/") = "https://gno.land/r/gnoland/" | rewritten realm page: Browse | TestReachDirListingBranchIsDead: no crawled URL can end in '/', so urlToFile's _dir branch ("r/gnoland/_dir/index.html") is unreachable

candidates.summary: hitting MaxPages returns an error that throws away every page already captured, so the whole preview is lost instead of truncated
candidates.failure_scenario: Run() checks `len(c.pages) >= c.MaxPages` before each fetch and returns `page cap %d reached`. main.go:134 does `if err := c.Run(); err != nil { return err }`, so Write is never called: the 400 pages already rendered by gnodev are discarded, no preview.json or comment.md is written, gnopreview exits 1 and the pr-preview job goes red with no preview comment. The cap is meant to bound work and instead voids it. Reachable because the ":args" URL space is ungated (see the inScope candidate): 400 pages are consumed from one realm whose render emits nested :arg links.
candidates.verify_by: go test -run TestReachColonArgsAreUngated -v . in misc/gnopreview; expect the cap to truncate the crawl and the captured pages to survive, observe an error and every page dropped
candidates.evidence: Run() error: page cap 400 reached (queue still had 397) | gnodev requests served: 400, pages captured then discarded: 400. At MaxPages=2: "page cap 2 reached (queue still had 2)", pages captured before the abort: 2, order: [/r/gnoland/home /r/gnoland/home$source]

candidates.summary: explosiveArgs gates the $query key space while the :args space has no gate at all
candidates.failure_scenario: inScope rejects oid/tid/download/func/state only inside the `$` query. The `:args` half of a gnoweb URL is passed through untouched: every `/r/<realm>:<anything>` link on a captured page is enqueued. gno.land realms emit exactly those - boards2 renders `/r/gnoland/boards2/v0:test-board/1/reply`, `:test-board/1/edit`, `:test-board/1/flag`, `:test-board/1/repost`, `:TestBoard/create-thread` (examples/gno.land/r/gnoland/boards2/v0/filetests/z_ui_reply_00_filetest.gno:55), valopers renders `/r/gnops/valopers:<address>` per validator (valopers.gno:469), commondao renders `/r/nt/commondao/v0:<id>` per DAO. A realm with seeded state whose render links per-item pages is crawled until the page cap, and the cap then discards the run. The fresh gnodev chain limits this today for realms with no init data; a realm that seeds state in init(), or the PR's own realm, is not limited.
candidates.verify_by: c.inScope("/r/gnoland/boards2/v0:test-board/1/reply") returns true with no per-realm arg budget anywhere in crawl.go; grep crawl.go for a cap on args and find only GnowebFileBudget, which gates `file=` alone
candidates.evidence: TestReachColonArgsAreUngated: inScope accepted the nested :arg link and the crawl consumed the full 400-page cap from a single realm; gnodev requests served: 400

candidates.summary: Run() resets c.pages but not c.order, so a reused Crawler nil-derefs in writePages
candidates.failure_scenario: Run() starts with `c.pages = map[string]*page{}` and leaves c.order holding the previous run's keys. writePages:327-329 walks c.order and dereferences `c.pages[u].File`, so any key from the earlier run that the new run did not re-capture (a page that started answering 404) panics with a nil pointer dereference and takes the whole render down. Latent today - main.go builds a fresh Crawler for the head and for the base - but the reset is half-written and the next caller that reuses one pays for it.
candidates.verify_by: go test -run TestReachSecondRunNilDerefs -v . in misc/gnopreview: two Run() calls where one URL 404s the second time, then writePages
candidates.evidence: order after one run: 4, after two: 7, pages: 3 | writePages panicked on the stale order entry: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference

candidates.summary: urlToFile's _dir branch cannot run, and two tests pin a collision that cannot occur
candidates.failure_scenario: listing is `strings.HasSuffix(base, "/") && base != "/"`, but no crawled URL can end in a slash: Seeds() builds every URL from urlOf and path.Dir, neither of which leaves one, and inScope:191 returns false for any trailing-slash link. So parts never gets "_dir" and no file is written through that branch. TestURLToFileIsSafe's "/r/x/y" vs "/r/x/y/" collision case and TestSplitURLKeepsTrailingSlash guard a shape the crawler never produces, which reads as coverage of the directory-listing path while the real directory link is the one going offsite.
candidates.verify_by: go test -run TestReachDirListingBranchIsDead -v . : assert inScope("/r/gnoland/") and that no Seeds() entry ends in "/"
candidates.evidence: no crawled URL can end in '/', so urlToFile's _dir branch ("r/gnoland/_dir/index.html") is unreachable
